item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-5bdeb5107ca757b8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that under Sisi, authorities systematically repressed critics and human rights defenders, thousands remained detained in lengthy pretrial detention or after unjust trials, and civic space was severely curtailed by judicial and security harassment.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes 2025 conditions, not 2023; relevant only as evidence of continuing institutional patterns during Sisi’s rule.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conditions to Sisi’s government and Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["Post-period source; no direct 2023 event is specified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5bdeb5107ca757b8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that the government failed to adequately fund education and health care, undermining economic and social rights.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes 2025 budgetary conditions rather than 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the funding decisions to the government under Sisi.","limitations":["Post-period evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5bdeb5107ca757b8","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Egypt’s parliamentary elections were held without real competition; the elections authority eliminated all party lists except one dominated by pro-Sisi parties and disqualified almost 200 individual candidates.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes 2025 elections, outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the electoral environment and pro-Sisi dominance to Sisi’s government.","limitations":["Post-period source and event."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5bdeb5107ca757b8","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that authorities used detainee ‘recycling,’ remote pretrial-detention hearings, mass terrorism trials, and weak fair-trial safeguards; Sisi initially rejected a flawed Criminal Procedure Code draft but later signed the bill after Parliament approved it with limited changes.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Describes 2025 events and later legislative action, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the rejection and signing decisions to Sisi and the detention practices to Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["Post-period evidence; the initial rejection is a qualifying favorable fact, while enactment is adverse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69e71bb60482a94c","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that Egypt’s central bank undertook exchange-rate depreciation and raised policy rates from March 2022 to address trade deficits, capital reversal, and declining foreign-exchange buffers; it also described macroeconomic and energy-sector reforms and external-financing measures as supporting resilience.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Provides context from 2022 and earlier; no 2023-specific result is reported.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the measures to the Central Bank and Egyptian government institutions, not solely to Sisi.","limitations":["Indirect ruler attribution; source page is a publication index rather than a full monitor."]},{"source_id":"SRC-10e91003cc7068bf","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The Cambridge introduction states that Sisi was elected president in 2014 after the military removed Mohamed Morsi, following Egypt’s first free and fair elections since the 1950s, and that a new Parliament was elected in 2015.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Historical background from 2012–2016, not a 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The account identifies the military’s removal of Morsi and Sisi’s subsequent election.","limitations":["Introductory summary only; does not provide detailed evidence about 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that authorities criminalized dissent and peaceful assembly, targeted journalists and opposition figures, and detained people for criticizing the government; it also reported that President Sisi ordered development of a national human rights strategy for the first time.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Describes 2025, outside the target period; the strategy announcement is a distinct favorable institutional action.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty directly attributes the strategy order to Sisi and the repression to Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["Post-period source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that security forces used enforced disappearance, incommunicado detention, torture, and ill-treatment against political detainees; it also reported arbitrary detention of Gaza March supporters and foreign participants.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.6","3B.1","3B.2","3B.8","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes 2025 events, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Egyptian security forces and prosecution authorities under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["Post-period evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Parliament approved amendments to the Code of Criminal Procedure that added alternatives to pretrial detention, but Amnesty found the amendments inconsistent with international law, especially regarding legal representation during questioning; Sisi ratified the bill in November.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2025 legislative action, outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"Sisi ratified the bill; Parliament enacted it.","limitations":["Post-period evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that impunity persisted for unlawful killings, torture, enforced disappearance, and other grave violations, with prosecutors dismissing or ignoring most torture complaints; in a rare case, a prosecutor referred one detainee for forensic examination but had not allowed his lawyer to review the report by year-end.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes 2025 and prior years, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern prosecution and security institutions under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["Post-period source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that the government failed to meet constitutional allocations of at least 3 percent of GDP for health and 6 percent for education; cash-transfer spending increased but remained inadequate to lift all recipients above the poverty line or reach everyone in need.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2025–2026 budget evidence, outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The allocations and social-protection policy are attributed to the Egyptian government.","limitations":["Post-period evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a545398e1db06e92","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In August, Sisi promulgated a bill repealing long-standing rent laws, ending decades-old rental contracts for about 1.6 million households after five or seven years; Amnesty reported inadequate consultation and uncertainty about compensation and affordability for low-income tenants.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.8","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2025 event, outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The bill was promulgated by Sisi.","limitations":["Post-period evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a7d44b5f81e4a31","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Since September 2023, Egyptian authorities carried out mass arrests of Sudanese refugees for irregular entry or stay, held them for days to six weeks in cruel conditions, and forcibly deported them without individualized risk assessment or an opportunity to claim asylum or challenge deportation.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers events beginning in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the arrests, detention, and deportations to Egyptian authorities under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The report does not identify Sisi’s personal order or involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1e2cc87ca6b6ca5c","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty’s UPR submission evaluated Egypt’s failure to implement recommendations concerning expression, association, assembly, torture, arbitrary detention, unfair trials, the death penalty, discrimination, impunity, and cooperation with UN mechanisms.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Prepared in 2024 for the January 2025 UPR; it evaluates implementation over the preceding period but gives no specific 2023 event in the supplied extract.","ruler_attribution":"The submission assesses state policy and institutional compliance under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["Summary page only; no detailed findings or dates are supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-cbe2d35a53b096d9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Since September 2023, Egyptian border guards and police carried out mass arbitrary arrests of Sudanese people fleeing conflict, including women, men, and children, detained them in warehouses or horse stables in cruel conditions, and forcibly returned them without access to asylum procedures or deportation challenges.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers events beginning in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Egypt’s Border Guard Forces and police under Sisi’s government.","limitations":["No direct evidence of Sisi’s personal instruction is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6b36403398711a5d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that Sisi said in a September 2023 speech that hunger and deprivation were acceptable sacrifices for development and progress.","question_ids":["3B.3","5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","7B.1","8B.1"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly identifies a September 2023 presidential statement.","ruler_attribution":"The statement is directly attributed to Sisi.","limitations":["The supplied extract does not provide the full speech or subsequent policy details."]},{"source_id":"SRC-96a622ef17097898","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"An ECFR report described Sisi’s regime as spending heavily on megaprojects and military equipment it considered unnecessary, associating this with reduced investment, rising poverty, and youth unemployment; it also described intensified repression, prison construction, torture, lethal force against protesters, and restrictions on expression and assembly.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.8","3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2017 assessment of earlier Sisi policies; not 2023-specific.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the spending and repression to Sisi’s regime.","limitations":["Analytical report by named authors; several claims are evaluative and predate the target period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9dd4ce92d7bb3b9","start_unit":4,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Sisi’s security forces escalated arrests and intimidation of opponents and critics; used counterterrorism and emergency laws; operated with near-absolute impunity; carried out arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, torture, unfair trials, mass executions, website blocking, restrictions on civil society, and collective punishment and displacement in North Sinai.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Describes events in 2018, outside the target period, but records institutional patterns under Sisi.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policies and conduct to Sisi’s government, security forces, and state institutions.","limitations":["Historical evidence rather than 2023-specific evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9dd4ce92d7bb3b9","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported two favorable but limited policy actions: Egypt passed a disability-rights law and comprehensive health-insurance law, while a national Hepatitis C program achieved substantial progress; implementation by-laws for the disability law had not yet been adopted.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2018 evidence, outside the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The laws and national health program are attributed to the Egyptian government under Sisi.","limitations":["No 2023 outcome evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9150e496293c740c","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Stephen J. King’s chapter states that Egypt’s military used conflicts between Islamists and secularists during the transition to stage a coup and reassert its dominance over the political economy; it also notes that Sisi’s election followed that military intervention.","question_ids":["2B.2","4B.1","4B.2","4B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Historical analysis of 2011–2013 events, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The account attributes the military intervention and subsequent political order to the Egyptian military and identifies Sisi as its beneficiary.","limitations":["Book chapter summary, not a detailed account of 2023."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["Most supplied sources concern years before or after 2023; facts were retained when they described a 2023 event or a concrete institutional pattern materially relevant to the questions.","The supplied extracts are often summary pages or publication indexes, so personal direction by Sisi cannot be inferred where only state or security-force conduct is reported."]}
